lesson-environment-management-environmen.quote: - **Special waste** includes household hazardous waste, such as paint, thinner, batteries, and spray canisters.

general-information-environment-manageme.quote: Keeping recyclable and reusable materials separate makes recycling and reuse easier, while special waste can be handled apart from ordinary waste.
general-information-environment-manageme.note: The rewrite explains why segregation supports recycling, and the recycling example shows collection followed by processing into recycled products.

general-information-environment-manageme.quote: A family washes an empty glass jar and uses it to store dry food. Which waste-diversion method is best shown?
general-information-environment-manageme.note: Reuse is now demonstrated in a worked scenario, and the core text also explains that separating reusable material makes reuse easier.

general-information-environment-manageme.quote: - **Compostable waste** is organic material that can break down through composting, such as food scraps and garden waste.
general-information-environment-manageme.note: The compostable category now has a definition, recognizable examples, and later composting teaching that shows where those materials go.

general-information-environment-manageme.quote: - **Recyclable waste** is material that can be recovered and processed for useful use, such as clean paper, glass, metal, or other accepted materials.
general-information-environment-manageme.note: The recyclable category now has a definition and examples, followed by a worked recycling scenario using clean paper.

general-information-environment-manageme.quote: - **Non-recyclable waste** is material that cannot be recovered through the available recycling or composting process and is not special waste.
general-information-environment-manageme.note: The non-recyclable category now has a sorting definition that distinguishes it from recoverable and special waste.

general-information-environment-manageme.quote: - **Special waste** includes household hazardous waste, such as paint, thinner, batteries, and spray canisters.
general-information-environment-manageme.note: Special waste is now defined with concrete examples and reinforced by a worked battery-sorting scenario.

general-information-environment-manageme.quote: An office replaces single-use drinking cups with washable cups that employees can use every day. Which waste-diversion method is best shown?
general-information-environment-manageme.note: Waste reduction is now demonstrated in a worked scenario where disposable cups are prevented from becoming waste.

general-information-environment-manageme.quote: A family washes an empty glass jar and uses it to store dry food. Which waste-diversion method is best shown?
general-information-environment-manageme.note: Reuse is now demonstrated through using the same jar again without processing it into a new material.

general-information-environment-manageme.note: Recycling is now demonstrated through collection and processing of used paper into recycled products.
